en: Title: Mahāsamājasūtra Source: Waldschmidt 1980 (revised edition), with standardizations Input: Péter-Dániel Szántó (3 July 2023, Budapest)
% NB Vāgīśvarakīrti’s *Mṛtyuvañcanopadeśa* (ed. Schneider 146–147, vv. 3.23–24):
The *Mahāsamāja-sūtra*, likewise the *Āṭānāṭīyaka*, The *Sūkṣmaka*, the *Mahāmegha*, and the verses known as the *Susvasti*.
One should cause the monks to recite it with due honor, or recite it oneself;
having thereby attained a long life, one becomes a deceiver of death.
That is to say, this sūtra remained popular and was recited for the sake of longevity.
Note: Schøyen MS 2382/272 is a fragment of a commentary.

[1] Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the Śākyas in the forest of Kapilavastu together with five hundred monks, all of whom were arhats—whose taints were exhausted, who had accomplished their task, completed what was to be done, laid down the burden, attained their own goal, utterly destroyed the fetters of existence, and whose minds were well-liberated through right knowledge. There, the Blessed One delivered a discourse on the Dharma concerning Nirvana to the community of monks. Furthermore, the great Śākya deities of the ten great world-systems, the Mahāśākyas, had assembled there and were attending upon the Blessed One and the community of monks.

[2] Then, it occurred to four deities dwelling in the Brahma-world belonging to the retinue of Brahmā: "Today, indeed, the Blessed One is staying among the Śākyas in the forest of Kapilavastu together with five hundred monks, all of whom are Arhats—as previously described—along with the community of monks. What if we were to go and, each individually, praise the Blessed One and the community of monks with verses?"

[3] Then four deities belonging to the Brahma-realm—just as a strong man might extend his drawn-in arm or draw in his extended arm—even so did the four deities of the Brahma-realm vanish from the Brahma-world and appear before the Blessed One. Standing to one side, one deity of the Brahma-realm at that time spoke this verse: “A great assembly has gathered on the slope; the hosts of gods have come together.
We have indeed come to behold the unconquerable Saṅgha.”
A second deity belonging to the Brahmakāyika realm spoke this verse:
"With minds made straight, the monks here apply themselves;
indeed, like a charioteer taking up the reins, they guard their sense faculties."
A third deity from the Brahmakāyika realm spoke this verse:
"Having indeed uprooted the stake,
he shall remove the Indra-stake, the crossbar, and the moat."
They move about pure and stainless,
tamed by the Leader like young elephants.
The fourth deity of the Brahmakāyika realm spoke this verse:
"Those who go for refuge to the Buddha do not go to an evil rebirth;
having cast off human bodies, they dwell in divine bodies."
Having spoken thus, the four deities belonging to the Brahma-realm vanished on that very spot.

[4] Then the Blessed One, having surveyed the entire assembly of gods, addressed the monks: "O monks, this gathering of deities is indeed very great; O monks, this gathering of deities in my assembly is indeed very great. Even for those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Awakened Ones of the past, the gathering of deities for those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, was as large as this gathering in my assembly now. I shall speak to you, monks; I will proclaim the names of the deities. Listen to what I say."
Resorting to gods and humans, up to the realm of Brahmā, they are destroyers of death.
The trainees (*śaikṣas*) announced [the name] "Two hundred and fifty," and another hundred and ten;
many thousands of deities proclaimed it,
while some clearly manifested throughout all directions even the name "Infinite" (*ananta*).
[6] Having understood them through his supernormal knowledge and having surveyed them, the Tathāgata,
the Teacher, then addressed the disciples who delight in the teaching.
The hosts of gods have approached; listen, O monks! I shall declare their names to you in succession through verses. Having become single-minded, hear what I say.
Seven thousand yakṣas, having illuminated the forest of Kapilavastu, remain stationed within that forest of Kapilavastu.
They too have come to this assembly, as well as those who share their sphere of activity—
possessing supernatural power, radiant, beautiful, and renowned—
who have approached and pay homage to the assembly of monks in the forest.
[8] Sātāgiri, extending across the three-thousandfold world system—
having illuminated it, he remains in the forest of Kapilavastu.
He too arrived at the assembly, as did those who were his companions, as described before;
six thousand from the Himalayas, all of various complexions, remained there, illuminating the forest of Kapilavastu.
And those who have come to the assembly, as well as their companions, are as described before. Thus,
these sixteen thousand yakṣas, all of various complexions,
having illuminated the forest of Kapilavastu, remain there.
They too have come to this assembly, as well as those who share their sphere of activity, as previously described.
Viśvāmitra with his five hundred followers and the greatly powerful Viśvadeva remain there, illuminating the forest of Kapilavastu.
They too have come to this assembly, as well as those who share their sphere of activity, as described before.
Furthermore, the yakṣa Kumbhīra, a resident of this vast Rājagṛha,
is attended by a hundred thousand yakṣas.
And they too have come to the assembly as before.
[13] In the eastern direction dwells the king, the Great King;
he is the king Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the lord of the Gandharvas by name.
Accompanied by his kinsmen, he always delights in dance and song;
and he too has arrived at the assembly as before.
[14] He is the King, the Great King, who protects the southern quarter.
The king who is the lord of the kumbhāṇḍas is named Virūḍhaka;
he always delights in dance and song together with his kinsmen.
He, too, arrived at the assembly as before.
[15] In the western direction, the Great King Virūpākṣa, the king and sovereign lord of the nāgas, by name, protects;
he always delights in dance and song together with his kinsmen.
He too has arrived at the assembly as before;
he is the King, the Great King, who protects the northern direction,
the sovereign of the yakṣas named Kubera.
He always delights in dance and song together with his kinsmen;
and he too arrived at the assembly as before.
[17] Dhṛtarāṣṭra is in the east, and Virūḍhaka is in the south.
In the west is Virūpākṣa, and Kubera is in the northern direction.
These four great kings, the illustrious guardians of the world, possess great supernatural power and great strength; they protect the four directions.
They too arrived at the assembly as before.
Their servants—deceitful, fraudulent, and crafty—arrived as well:
Māyāvin, Kiṭi, and Vikiṭi, along with Bhṛgu and Bhṛkuṭinyā.
Displaying their miraculous powers at that time in Saṃbahula-caitrika, they too arrived at the assembly as before.

These Yakṣas, Mahāyakṣas, and Yakṣa generals who lead the army also entered here; namely Indra, Soma, Varuṇa, Prajāpati, and so forth, as previously described in the case of Aṭānāṭika, up to Triphalī and Trikaṇṭhakī. They too arrived at the assembly as before.
[20] The Naga Sahabhū has arrived, as have Vaiśāla and Takṣaka;
Kambalāśvatara has come, along with Prajāgu and Guṇa.
Saudāsaka Dhṛtarāṣṭra—[and] the lordly elephants:
the illustrious Airāvaṇa, the great and formidable elephant, has arrived before me...
and they too have come to this assembly as before.
[21] That powerful twice-born bird of pure vision, who by force seizes the Naga king,
has come to the forest through the air.
"Citra Suvarṇī" was his name.
There, the well-winged one, having become Suparṇita, granted fearlessness to the Naga kings;
the Teacher brought about their security with gentle and joyful words.
Right there, he went for refuge to the Buddha.
And he too arrived at the assembly as before.
[22] The Asuras dwelling in the ocean were conquered by the wielder of the thunderbolt (Vajrapāṇi).
Sucitra, Vemacitra, Prahlāda, and likewise Mucila;
and the hundred sons of Baḍi, all of whom were named Vairocana.
"Indeed, Rāhu has approached the auspicious army of the Bāḍis;
it is now time for you, O Great Hero, to go to the assembly of monks in the forest."
They too arrived at the assembly as before;
Varuṇā and Vāruṇī, as well as Kṣaumā, followed behind,
and the illustrious goddess Maitrī and Varuṇikā also arrived.
The earth and the gods, the waters and the god Vāyu, and Pāvaka the fire—
these ten bodies of ten each, all possessing diverse colors,
remain illuminating the forest of Kapilavastu.
And they too arrived at the assembly as before;
the god Viṣṇu, the god Sahalī, and Yama arrived—
along with the gods who are followers of Candra, placing Candra at their head.
The gods of the Sūryopaniṣad, placing the sun at their head and placing the constellations at their head, arrived as the clouds grew feeble;
Maghavat, the powerful Purandara, arrived with all [his hosts].
These ten groups of ten bodies are as before.
[25] The goddess Sabhikā has arrived, resembling a crest of blazing flames;
and Ariṣṭikā, Romā, Umā, and Puṣpanivāsinī.
The Carakas, with girdles firmly fastened, are many times unshakable;
Pradyumna and Svātikā have reached that direction which rains down [upon them].
These ten groups of ten bodies are as before.
Śuklā, Kaḍambā, Karuṇā, Prāptā, and Nīlakavāsinī; Avadātakeśā, Pramukhī, Prāptā, and Pītakavāsinī.
The Sadāmattas, Hāritakas, and Miśrikas in great numbers,
as well as the Śuddhakas and Rucikas— these illustrious gods have arrived.
These ten groups of ten bodies are as previously described. [27] [28] Furthermore, there are the Kṣemakas, Tuṣitas, Yāmas, and Kṛṣṇuktas in great numbers.
Lumbinī, Lumbinīśreṣṭhā, and Jyotis by name, through their own aspirations; the Nirmāṇaratis and also the Vaśavartins—
these ten groups of ten bodies are as previously described.
[29] Indeed, ten lords have been attained, each exercising sovereign power over a thousand Brahma-worlds; he is called Mahābrahmā,
along with Sanatkumāra and Tiṣya, together with their sons who possess miraculous powers.
They too arrived at the assembly as before;
and following behind them came Hāritī Vaśavartinī,
supreme in complexion and form, surrounded by her sons.
She too came to the assembly as before;
and all these gods, including Indra, Īśāna, and Prajāpati, have arrived.
The monks also have arrived here—behold the counsel of Kṛṣṇa!
"Take this, bind it, and may prosperity be yours!
Having surrounded him on all sides with loving-kindness, release him alive."
Thus there Mahāsena Kṛṣṇa urged on his army;
and he himself, though enraged and no longer master of himself, also turned back toward the fray.
Striking the earth with his hand and making a most terrifying sound,
he then caused the cloud-mass together with lightning to rain down from the sky.
[32] Having known them through his supernormal knowledge and having observed them, the Tathāgata,
the Teacher, then addressed the disciples who delight in the teaching.
"O monks, listen as Māra’s army advances!
Having heard these words spoken by the Buddha,
even those who practice with ardor do not have a single hair on their bodies quiver, for they regard him as one who is truly free from passion.
And those sons of the Victors, the disciples, having conquered in battle, fearless and renowned, rejoice together with their followers.
[33] Thus spoke the Blessed One; with uplifted minds, those monks rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.
The intermediate summary verse: Varuṇa, Viṣṇu, Sabhika, Śukla, Śyāma, and the Kṣemakas.
The Mahāsamāja Sūtra is finished; it is truly completed. Well done!
